Cc: ops@aurora-bio.com
Date: Wed, 08 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial capacity ask: burst headroom for gen-heavy workloads

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow-up from our infra/ML team: we expect a phased rollout that starts with 100 concurrent gen sessions (avg 1.2k tokens/session) and then a marketing surge in month 3 that could spike to ~700 concurrent sessions for 6–12 hours/day.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood guarantee a burst headroom policy so we maintain <150ms p95 for short requests during surges?
- What does the autoscale ramp look like for Dedicated (reserved pool + ephemeral burst) and how quickly can we add GPUs without manual intervention?

Attached is an estimated traffic profile and a simple capacity matrix. We need this answered ahead of our architecture review on Monday.

Thanks,
Tim
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Aurora BioSciences

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Li <tim.li@aurora-bio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Mar 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask: burst headroom for gen-heavy workloads

Hi Tim — great to see the traffic profile, that helps a lot. High level answers up front, details below:

1) Burst headroom and latency SLOs
- For Dedicated customers we recommend reserving a baseline slab sized for steady-state (we’d size ~80 GPUs for your initial 100 concurrent sessions at 1.2k tokens avg).
- We support a two-tier burst model: (A) short-lived ephemeral headroom from a pre-warmed shoulder pool (seconds-to-minutes) and (B) elastic slab expansion that takes ~10–12 minutes to provision additional reserved nodes (depends on image warm-up and KV cache population).
- Short-lived headroom (shoulder pool) is tuned to preserve p95 latency under short surges; for your profile we can target p95 < 200ms with the shoulder pool alone, and <150ms if we combine a small pre-warmed slot of quantized instances (Q4_0.8 profiles).

2) Autoscale policy and guardrails
- Policy template we propose: target_util=65%, max_burst_ratio=2.5x, scale_cooldown=90s, slab_expand_threshold=3m sustained above target_util.
- Eviction policy: preemptible/ephemeral nodes are reclaimed preferentially; user-reserved capacity is preserved.
- Canary fallback: requests routed to an earlier-quantized variant if new slab nodes fail to come up.

3) Ops and runbook items
- We’ll provide a ramp playbook with traffic gates and synthetic probe checks (latency, model-perf regression, memory pressure).
- Suggested sequencing: 1) shoulder pool (pre-warmed) -> 2) bump autoscale aggressiveness on sustained load -> 3) expand reserved slab if sustained > 48 hours.

I attached a draft playbook and a quick capacity matrix mapping concurrency -> GPUs by model family. If helpful, we can run a short live surge test next week.

Cheers,
Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood-burst-playbook-draft.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Li <tim.li@aurora-bio.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Mar 2028 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask: burst headroom for gen-heavy workloads

Tim / Karthik — thanks. From a commercial perspective we can include a scoped burst allowance in the Dedicated contract: 200% of baseline for incidental surges (no additional commit), plus an option for paid overage at a discounted uplift for sustained expansions.

To confirm: baseline will be the reserved slab (billing commit). Shoulder pool and ephemeral bursts are included as operational protections and not billed against the commit unless sustained > 48 hours. If Aurora wants guaranteed <150ms p95 during peak marketing events we should model an explicit pre-warmed quantized slice (14-day minimum) which would sit on top of the baseline and be billed as part of the reserved commit.

I'll align with Finance and prepare a redline for the SOW. Karthik / Monica — can you validate the GPU counts so I can finalize pricing?

—Ben
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Aurora burst provisioning — plan & action items

Team — internal checklist after the Aurora sync. Pulling together the playbook and runbook for commercial SOW and ops onboarding. Action items: 

- Neha: validate the thermal/warmup assumptions for Q4_0.8 on A100-80GB and quantize fallback variant. Confirm realistic slab expand times with infra (target 10–12m).
- Monica: map customer regions to our US-hosted Dedicated POPs and confirm cross-region fallback latency impact.
- Ben: include the pre-warmed quantized slice as an optional line item in the SOW and price both 14-day and 90-day commits.
- Karthik (me): schedule surge test window + synthetic probe suite; draft handoff doc for Aurora SREs.

I'll produce a consolidated playbook PDF and a one-page ops checklist by EOD Monday. We should also include a simple drill: failover to quantized variant + degraded model to validate the canary fallback.

-Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
